# Strata Property Regulation

*Strata Property Regulation*, BC Reg 43/2000 (made under the Strata Property Act), verbatim from the BC Laws consolidation, one item per section. Licence `bc-kings-printer`. Every item here is generated by `tools/import-bclaws.ts`; do not edit the text by hand.

## Layout

```
source.json                   the regulation: citation, urls, consolidation ("current to") date,
                              retrieved_at, parts[] with sections, omitted[], not_imported[]
part-01/ … part-17/           one folder per Part with current sections; s<section>.md per section
part-05.1/  part-05.2/        Parts 5.1 and 5.2 keep their published numbers
```

Parts 2 and 15 have no sections ("[No Sections]" on BC Laws), and every section of Parts 8 and 18 is repealed, so those Parts have no folder. `source.json` still lists them.

## Id scheme

Regulation sections are numbered `<Part>.<n>`, and later insertions add digits: 6.2, then 6.21, 6.22 and 6.23; 5.1, then 5.101; 3.01 before 3.1. Each of these is a **separate section**, not a subsection. So:

- The id is `bc.spr.s` plus the section number exactly as BC Laws prints it: `bc.spr.s6.2`, `bc.spr.s6.21`, `bc.spr.s5.101`, `bc.spr.s3.01`. Never normalise the number (6.21 is not 6.2 subsection 1; 3.01 is not 3.1).
- Ids never name a subsection or paragraph. Subsection (1) of section 6.2 is the `## (1)` heading inside `bc.spr.s6.2`, reached through the chunk heading path (`section_ref`), never an id like `bc.spr.s6.2.1`.
- `citation` is `Strata Property Regulation, BC Reg 43/2000, s 6.2`. `source_url` is `…/statreg/43_2000#section6.2`. File: `part-06/s6.2.md`.

## Body format

As for the Act (see `law/bc/acts/strata-property-act/README.md`): `# Section 7.1 — Maximum fines`, `## (1)` per subsection, nested `- (a)` list items, defined terms bold in quotes, whitespace normalised, words and punctuation exact. In addition:

- The history note BC Laws prints at the end of a section (for example `[en. B.C. Reg. 162/2018; am. B.C. Reg. 6/2023, s. 1.]`) is kept as the last paragraph, exactly as published. It records which regulations enacted or amended the section.
- **Formulas.** Sections 6.4, 6.5, 11.2 and 11.3 contain formulas that BC Laws publishes as small tables of text (a fraction bar and a multiplier). The item lays each formula out as plain text inside a ```` ```text ```` block, arranged like the page; every word is kept, and `notes` flag the layout for review.

## Repealed sections, and the Schedule of Forms

- Whole repealed sections are **not imported**; they are listed in `source.json` `omitted[]` with the placeholder text BC Laws shows: 6.12, 6.13, 8.1–8.3, 17.5, 17.14, 17.15 and 18.1.
- The **Schedule of Forms (Forms A to Z.1) is imported**, as 27 items under `forms/`, ids `bc.spr.form.<letter>`. What is imported is the prescribed form *content* in the Regulation, which the King's Printer Licence covers; the government's own fillable form products are a separate thing the licence excludes (cl. 8.1(a), open question 15), and nothing here is a substitute for filing one.
  - Every word is kept, in published order. The layout is simplified: a table is one line per row with cells separated by `" | "`, a tick box is `[ ]`, and a rule dividing one part of a form from the next is `---`. A form item answers *what the form asks for and in what words*, not *what the form looks like on the page*, and each item's `notes` says so.
  - The only image in the Schedule is the 12px tick-box, written as `[ ]` rather than linked. Any other graphic stops the import: a diagram or a Provincial symbol must not pass silently, and the licence does not cover the coat of arms or government logos (cl. 4.1).
  - **Form J is repealed** (B.C. Reg. 6/2023, s. 7) and still occupies its letter. It is imported as `bc.spr.form.j` with the published "Repealed." text, so a question about Form J is answered rather than met with silence. `in_force_to` is `null`: the consolidation does not give the date the repeal took effect.
  - `cites[]` on a form comes from the reference BC Laws prints under its name, not from `pnpm link:cites`. That reference says plainly which sections are the Act's and which the Regulation's — a bare "Section 59" inside a Regulation item would otherwise be read as the Regulation's section 59, which is the wrong enactment.
  - Forms are listed in `source.json` `forms[]`.

## Dates

- `consolidation_date` in `source.json` is the BC Laws "current to" date; `retrieved_at` is the fetch date. The regulation itself was deposited February 4, 2000, effective July 1, 2000, and was last amended May 11, 2026 by B.C. Reg. 79/2026 (from the BC Laws page).
- `in_force_from` is `null` on every item, with a note: the consolidation does not say when each section's current text came into force (the history note names the amending regulations, not their effective dates for that section). `in_force_to` is `null`.

## Refreshing

```sh
pnpm --dir kb import:bclaws            # fetches …/statreg/43_2000/xml and the page …/statreg/43_2000
pnpm --dir kb import:bclaws --offline  # rebuild from kb/.cache/bclaws/
pnpm --dir kb validate && pnpm --dir kb build
```

Behaviour on re-runs (kept review sign-off, changed text back to draft, topics from `tools/lib/bclaws-topics.ts`) is described in the Act's README.
